title: AA Batteries 8-pack

drivers.name: Price increase (5.5%)
drivers.evidence: Two recent weeks at $10.81 had median sales 12% below baseline (31.0 vs 34.9); consistent with price sensitivity.

drivers.name: Store closure (Monday)
drivers.evidence: One day of closure reduces selling time by 20%; no similar past closure data, so effect assumed linear.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 34.9. The target week has no event but a 5.5% price increase to $10.81 (above regular $10.25) and a store closure on Monday. Recent weeks at the higher price (10.81) show a median of 31.0 (vs baseline 34.9), a 12% drop. This aligns with the 2026-09-28 and 2026-10-05 data. The closure of Monday reduces the selling window by 20%, likely lowering sales. No promotion or event supports uplift. The classical model suggests no effect, but the price increase and closure are known drivers. The evidence for price impact is consistent across two weeks. The closure effect is estimated at -20% from reduced operating days. Combined, the median is adjusted down by ~16%, with moderate uncertainty due to limited past closure data.

brief:
PRODUCT: AA Batteries 8-pack | category Household | Store #12 (Austin, TX)
TARGET WEEK: 2026-11-09 to 2026-11-15 (5 weeks after the last week with sales data)

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: none
  shelf price: 10.81 (+5.5% vs regular price 10.25)
  planner notes: Store closed Monday for renovation

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 34.9 | 5%-95%: 18.5 - 58.2 | 10%-90%: 20.9 - 55.2

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-44% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
